members.name: SET_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_STATE
members.description: The browser layer reports one stored credential's registry state — usable, needs sign-in, or refresh failed. Registry fact only; the sealed material never crosses, and absence is expressed by FORGET_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL rather than by a state.

members.name: PROBE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL
members.description: Prove one pasted or stored key by a single bounded completion (decision 0083). The core composes the cheapest probe call for the provider outside any task; the handle may be a one-shot transient the browser spends exactly once, so the probe effect is never retried.

members.name: SUPPLY_FIELD_VALUES
members.description: The person answered a request to fill a form in (decision 0088). It reports how many values they supplied and nothing else: what they typed was minted into the browser's vault and never crossed, so there is nothing here to hold and nothing derived from one either. A count of zero is an answer and not a refusal.

members.name: SET_PROVIDER_MODEL_PREFERENCE
members.description: One person's standing choice of model and thinking level for one provider, stated whole. The browser owns the file this is replayed from at start-up, exactly as it owns the credential state beside it; the core validates the model against the merged catalog and refuses a pin it does not carry rather than storing a name nothing can route to.

enums.name: FieldValueAskOutcome
enums.description: What became of one request for values, stated as the next move it implies rather than as the browser clause it came from (decision 0215). The browser's fourteen abandonment clauses and its capture's eleven refusal clauses keep their own granularity in the device log and fold into these seven on the way out, because a clause is a fact about the browser's internals and a member here is an instruction. Closed and failing closed: a value this build does not recognise is refused, and the wire carries an integer, so nothing derived from a page can cross a boundary whose whole property is that it carries a count (decision 0088).

members.name: ANSWERED
members.description: The person filled the sheet in, and `supplied` is what they gave. Wire zero so that a command from before this field existed means what it always meant.

members.name: DISMISSED
members.description: The sheet was drawn and the person closed it without filling anything in. Asking the same way again asks them to refuse twice.

members.name: NOT_A_FIELD
members.description: The line the task named takes no value, so no sheet could be about it. The move is to name the form, or a line that takes text.

members.name: CHALLENGE_OFF_SCREEN
members.description: The challenge's picture is on the page and outside the part of it in view, so the browser had nothing to copy. The target was right and the page has to move: this is the one member whose next move is to scroll that number into view and ask again.

members.name: CANNOT_BE_SHOWN
members.description: The browser could not build a sheet for that field for some other reason: no picture it could copy, no outline to draw, no label, or a field list it could not hold.

members.name: PAGE_MOVED
members.description: The page changed while the request was being prepared or answered, so the ask no longer described anything. A fresh reading comes first.

members.name: NO_SURFACE
members.description: Nothing could draw a sheet at all: no bound surface, or no well-formed document in the tab. Asking again cannot help.

structs.name: CatalogFetchEffect
structs.description: Ask the browser to fetch the newest published catalog snapshot. Anonymous and content-free: no account, no device identifier, and no URL — the browser resolves the operation against its compiled origin, key and route, so a snapshot can never re-point the fetch that carries it.

structs.name: CatalogFetchEffectResult

fields.name: operation_kind
fields.description: Which catalog operation this answers.

fields.name: disposition

structs.name: CachedCatalogOverlay
structs.description: The served-catalog cache the browser kept from the last accepted fetch, handed back whole at bootstrap. Bytes and an instant, nothing more: the core re-judges both against its own age ceiling and fail-closed decode, so a stale, torn or hostile file degrades routing to the compiled baseline instead of corrupting it, and a refusal never fails the profile.

fields.name: fetched_at_utc_ms
fields.description: When the cached document was fetched, in UTC milliseconds. The freshness clock keeps counting from this instant, not from the reread, so a restart never extends a cache’s life.

fields.name: document
fields.description: The document bytes exactly as the origin served them. Interpreted only on the sandboxed Rust sequence, by the same decode and sanitize path a live fetch goes through.

structs.name: AssetOnDisk
structs.description: What the browser found on disk for one asset. Only the four facts a filesystem can answer: the core reconciles them against the catalog it was built with, and refuses a record naming an asset that catalog does not carry. Nothing here is a judgement, and nothing here is a field the browser would have to guess at.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.description: The asset's stable identity, as the staged or installed path spells it.

fields.name: asset_revision
fields.description: The revision found. A state for another revision says nothing about this one, so an upgrade is never mistaken for an install that is already done.

fields.name: presence
fields.description: How much of it is there. Never ABSENT: an asset with nothing on disk has no record.

fields.name: written_bytes
fields.description: Bytes on disk. For an installed artifact this is its size; for a staged one it is where the transfer got to.

structs.name: SkillRecord
structs.description: One bounded active-version skill row, restored whole at bootstrap or transiently validated as part of an isolated backup stage before commit authority. Staged validation installs nothing, restores no run history and starts no target runtime. The durable store still exposes no general query surface (OD-104).

fields.name: skill_id
fields.description: The skill's stable identity, minted by the core and shown to a person.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: The one canonical tuple origin this skill was written for. Same-origin and never same-site: a skill written for one origin has seen one origin's pages.

fields.name: provenance
fields.description: Where it came from. Not a permission.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where it is in the one lifecycle.

fields.name: active_version
fields.description: Which version the definition below is. Editing a skill in place does not exist; superseding it mints the next version.

fields.name: definition
fields.description: The bounded encoded steps and match condition of that version. The browser may check its bounded identity header, but only the sandboxed Core decodes and validates the complete portable language.

fields.name: step_count
fields.description: How many steps that version holds. Bounded at storage rather than truncated at replay, because a truncated skill is a different skill still claiming the original's identity.

fields.name: installed_at_utc_ms
fields.description: When the installation was first recorded.

fields.name: updated_at_utc_ms
fields.description: When its status or active version last moved.

structs.name: SkillRunRecord

fields.name: skill_id

fields.name: version
fields.description: Which version of it ran. A run names a version rather than a skill, because the steps are what an audit record has to be able to name.

fields.name: ran_at_utc_ms

structs.name: TaskFieldValuesEffect
structs.description: One open request to the person to fill a form in (decision 0088). It names the line the model asked about and, when that line is a field rather than a form, the other fields on the same page that only the person can supply (decision 0238), so one sheet asks for an identity number and a CAPTCHA's answer together. Nothing else inside the page is named: which of those fields still need a person, and what kind of thing each one is, is decided in the browser from the classification it re-reads at dispatch, because that is already the authority a fill is checked against and a second one would disagree exactly when it mattered. Nothing here is a value or is derived from one — no count of values, no length, no shape, no digest — because a form field's value comes from a domain small enough that a digest over it is the value (decision 0063 section 4). The node identities are the observation's own, which the core already held before the person typed anything.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: Durable request identity derived from the turn and the call that asked, so a replay re-opens the same request rather than a second one. It is also the name the browser mints each answer into its vault under, paired with the answer's position, so both processes agree on what a held value is called without either sending the other a name.

fields.name: tab_id
fields.description: The task-owned tab holding the form.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: The form the model named, as a handle from the observation it was reading. The browser resolves it and refuses a handle that no longer names a form.

fields.name: companion_node_ids
fields.description: The other fields on the same page and document that only the person can supply — an identity number, a one-time code, a CAPTCHA's answer — in page order, which the core asks about together with node_id when node_id names a field rather than a form (decision 0238): most sites draw their inputs with no form element around them, and a field named on its own was the only one the sheet asked about. Empty when node_id names a form, because the browser expands a form itself, and empty when there are none. Distinct, never node_id itself, each a bounded identifier, and never so many that node_id and these together exceed the sheet's MAX_TASK_SUPPLIED_VALUES rows. They are observation identities the core already held, never values and never derived from one. The browser re-reads each one at dispatch and asks only about those that still need a person; one that no longer resolves, or no longer needs a person, is left out of the sheet rather than refusing it.

structs.name: SupplyFieldValuesCommand
structs.description: What the browser reports when the person answered a request to fill a form in. It carries a count and, for each held value, the field it was minted for, and neither is a value: a held value is named by its request identity and its position, which both processes derive rather than exchange, so the core can compose a proposal naming the person's second answer without ever having been told what a held value is called, let alone what is in it. The field identities are what lets the core put each value into its field without a model turn between the answer and the fills (decision 0238). A count past the request's bound is refused rather than clamped.

fields.name: task_id
fields.description: The owning task.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: The request being answered. The reducer refuses an answer to a request it is not holding open, so a late or duplicated answer cannot resume a task that has moved on.

fields.name: supplied
fields.description: How many values the person supplied. Zero is admitted: a person who opened the surface and filled nothing in has answered, and the assistant has to learn that rather than wait on a surface that has already closed.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.description: Bounded browser-minted audit trace identity for the durable reducer command.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: What became of the ask (decision 0215). A zero `supplied` is not one fact but six, and each implies a different next move; sending only the count left the assistant to guess, and on the myAadhaar CAPTCHA it guessed 'ask again' eleven times over a picture that was merely below the fold. The member is chosen from the browser's own control flow and never from anything on the page, which is what keeps this crossing content-free.

fields.name: field_node_ids
fields.description: The field each held value was minted for, in position order: entry i is the field value i goes into, which is the order the browser's preapproval admits fills in (decision 0195). Exactly `supplied` entries, distinct, each a bounded identifier; any other shape is refused rather than repaired. They are the observation's own node identities, which the core already holds from the page it read and from the request it made — never a value, never derived from one, and chosen by which fields the sheet showed and never by what the person typed (decision 0063 section 4). The core fills value i into entry i through the ordinary proposal, policy and dispatch path (decision 0238).
